title.raw: 《蕭相國世家》 House of Chancellor Xiao

sentences.zh: 蕭相國何者，沛豐人也。

translations.literal: Prime Minister Xiao He was a man from Feng in Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Xiao He was a native of Feng in the district of Pei.

sentences.zh: 以文無害為沛主吏掾。

translations.literal: Through his mastery of documents and the law (wen wuhai), he became the chief clerk of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: His skill with documents and administrative competence earned him the position of chief clerk in Pei.

sentences.zh: 高祖為布衣時，何數以吏事護高祖。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was a commoner, He frequently used his official duties to protect Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Back when Gaozu was still a commoner, Xiao He often used his official position to shield him from trouble.

sentences.zh: 高祖為亭長，常左右之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became pavilion chief, He constantly assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu became a village headman, Xiao He was always at his side to help.

sentences.zh: 高祖以吏繇咸陽，吏皆送奉錢三，何獨以五。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was drafted as an official to Xianyang, all the officials presented three coins for the farewell feast, but He alone presented five.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was conscripted for labor service in Xianyang, every other official gave him three cash as a parting gift, but Xiao He alone gave five.

sentences.zh: 秦御史監郡者與從事，常辨之。

translations.literal: The Qin imperial secretary who supervised the commandery and worked with him always praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin imperial censor assigned to oversee the commandery always commended Xiao He after working alongside him.

sentences.zh: 何乃給泗水卒史事，第一。

translations.literal: He then served as clerk for the Sishui district, ranking first.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He went on to serve as a clerk in the Sishui commandery, where he was rated first among all his peers.

sentences.zh: 秦御史欲入言徵何，何固請，得毋行。

translations.literal: The Qin imperial secretary wished to enter and recommend summoning He, but He firmly declined and managed not to go.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin censor wanted to recommend him for a summons to the capital, but Xiao He firmly declined and managed to avoid the transfer.

sentences.zh: 及高祖起為沛公，何常為丞督事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu rose up to become Lord of Pei, He constantly served as deputy and oversaw affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose in rebellion and became the Lord of Pei, Xiao He served as his deputy and managed all administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 沛公至咸陽，諸將皆爭走金帛財物之府分之，何獨先入收秦丞相御史律令圖書藏之。

translations.literal: When the Lord of Pei reached Xianyang, all the generals rushed to the treasuries of gold, silk, and valuables to divide them up, but He alone first entered and collected the Qin chancellor's and imperial secretary's statutes, orders, maps, and books to store them away.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lord of Pei entered Xianyang, all the other generals raced to the treasuries to divide the gold, silk, and valuables among themselves. Xiao He alone went first to secure the Qin chancellor's and imperial censor's collections of laws, decrees, maps, and registers.

sentences.zh: 沛公為漢王，以何為丞相。

translations.literal: When the Lord of Pei became Han King, he made He chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lord of Pei was named King of Han, he appointed Xiao He as his chancellor.

sentences.zh: 項王與諸侯屠燒咸陽而去。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu and the feudal lords massacred and burned Xianyang and left.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu and the other lords sacked and burned Xianyang before departing.

sentences.zh: 漢王所以具知天下阸塞，戶口多少，彊弱之處，民所疾苦者，以何具得秦圖書也。

translations.literal: The reason the Han King fully knew the strategic passes of the realm, the number of households and population, the strong and weak places, and what the people suffered from was because He had obtained all the Qin maps and books.
translations.idiomatic: It was because Xiao He had secured the complete Qin archives that the King of Han came to know precisely where every strategic pass lay, how many households and people lived in each region, which areas were strong and which were weak, and what grievances the people bore.

sentences.zh: 何進言韓信，漢王以信為大將軍。

translations.literal: He recommended Han Xin, and the Han King made Xin grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He recommended Han Xin, and the King of Han appointed him as supreme general.

sentences.zh: 語在淮陰侯事中。

translations.literal: The words are in the affairs of Marquis Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: The details of this are recorded in the account of the Marquis of Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 漢王引兵東定三秦，何以丞相留收巴蜀，填撫諭告，使給軍食。

translations.literal: When the Han King led troops east to pacify the Three Qins, He as chancellor remained to collect Bashu, fill and pacify by proclamation and instruction, and supply the army with food.
translations.idiomatic: When the King of Han led his troops east to subdue the Three Qin kingdoms, Xiao He stayed behind as chancellor to secure Ba and Shu, pacifying the people with proclamations and keeping the army supplied with provisions.

sentences.zh: 漢二年，漢王與諸侯擊楚，何守關中，侍太子，治櫟陽。

translations.literal: In Han year 2, the Han King together with the feudal lords attacked Chu. He guarded Guanzhong, attended to the crown prince, and governed from Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Han, the King of Han joined the other lords in attacking Chu. Xiao He remained to guard the lands within the passes, attend the crown prince, and govern from Yueyang.

sentences.zh: 為法令約束，立宗廟社稷宮室縣邑，輒奏上，可，許以從事；

translations.literal: He established statutes and regulations, erected ancestral temples, altars of soil and grain, palaces, chambers, districts, and counties. Whenever he memorialized upward, if approved, he was permitted to proceed;
translations.idiomatic: He drafted laws and regulations, established ancestral temples, altars to the gods of soil and grain, palaces, and administrative districts. Whenever he submitted a memorial and it was approved, he was permitted to proceed.

sentences.zh: 即不及奏上，輒以便宜施行，上來以聞。

translations.literal: if there was no time to memorialize upward, he would proceed according to what was expedient, and report upward when the emperor came.
translations.idiomatic: When there was no time to wait for approval, he acted as he saw fit and reported the matter upon the emperor's return.

sentences.zh: 關中事計戶口轉漕給軍，漢王數失軍遁去，何常興關中卒，輒補缺。

translations.literal: Guanzhong affairs were calculated by households and population, transporting grain to supply the army. The Han King frequently lost troops and fled, but He constantly raised Guanzhong soldiers and promptly filled the gaps.
translations.idiomatic: He managed the affairs within the passes by tallying households and organizing grain shipments to supply the army. Each time the King of Han lost his forces and had to flee, Xiao He raised fresh troops from within the passes and promptly filled the gaps.

sentences.zh: 上以此專屬任何關中事。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore specially entrusted all Guanzhong affairs to He.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, the emperor entrusted Xiao He with sole authority over all affairs within the passes.

sentences.zh: 漢三年，漢王與項羽相距京索之閒，上數使使勞苦丞相。

translations.literal: In Han year 3, the Han King confronted Xiang Yu between Jing and Suo, and the emperor frequently sent envoys to console the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Han, while the King of Han faced Xiang Yu between Jing and Suo, the emperor repeatedly sent messengers to offer his regards to the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 鮑生謂丞相曰：「王暴衣露蓋，數使使勞苦君者，有疑君心也。

translations.literal: Bao Sheng told the chancellor: 'The king exposes himself to wind and dew, frequently sending envoys to console you—this shows doubt in his heart toward you.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Bao Sheng told the chancellor, 'The king endures hardship in the open field yet keeps sending messengers to inquire after you. This means he harbors suspicions about your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 為君計，莫若遣君子孫昆弟能勝兵者悉詣軍所，上必益信君。」

translations.literal: For your sake, nothing would be better than sending all your sons, grandsons, younger brothers who can bear arms to the army camp—the emperor will certainly trust you even more.'
translations.idiomatic: For your own sake, you should send every one of your sons, grandsons, and brothers who can bear arms to join the army at the front. The emperor will certainly trust you all the more for it.'

sentences.zh: 於是何從其計，漢王大說。

translations.literal: Thus He followed this plan, and the Han King was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He followed this advice, and the King of Han was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 漢五年，既殺項羽，定天下，論功行封。

translations.literal: In Han year 5, after killing Xiang Yu and pacifying the realm, they discussed merits and bestowed enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Han, after Xiang Yu had been slain and the realm pacified, the court debated each man's merits and awarded fiefs accordingly.

sentences.zh: 群臣爭功，歲餘功不決。

translations.literal: The ministers disputed over merits, and for more than a year the merits were not decided.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers quarreled over who deserved the most credit, and for more than a year no verdict was reached.

sentences.zh: 高祖以蕭何功最盛，封為酂侯，所食邑多。

translations.literal: Gaozu considered Xiao He's merit the greatest, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Cuo, with many fief households.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu judged Xiao He's contributions the greatest and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Zan, granting him the largest fief of all.

sentences.zh: 功臣皆曰：「臣等身被堅執銳，多者百餘戰，少者數十合，攻城略地，大小镑有差。

translations.literal: All the meritorious ministers said: 'We have worn armor and wielded sharp weapons, the many fought over a hundred battles, the few fought several dozen engagements, attacking cities and seizing territory, with distinctions between large and small contributions.
translations.idiomatic: The other ministers with war records protested, 'We have donned armor and taken up arms, fighting over a hundred battles at most and several dozen at least, storming cities and seizing territory, each with his own record of distinction.

sentences.zh: 今蕭何未嘗有汗馬之勞，徒持文墨議論，不戰，顧反居臣等上，何也？」

translations.literal: Now Xiao He has never had the labor of sweating horses, merely holding brush and ink to discuss affairs, not fighting, yet instead he ranks above us all—why is this?'
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xiao He has never once broken a sweat on horseback. All he did was wield a writing brush and talk. He never fought, and yet he is ranked above every one of us. How can this be?'

sentences.zh: 高帝曰：「諸君知獵乎？」

translations.literal: Gaozu said: 'Do you gentlemen know hunting?'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, 'Do you gentlemen know anything about hunting?'

sentences.zh: 曰：「知之。」

translations.literal: They said, 'We know it.'
translations.idiomatic: They replied, 'We do.'

sentences.zh: 「知獵狗乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, 'Do you know hunting dogs?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, 'Do you know about hunting dogs?'

sentences.zh: 曰：「知之。」

translations.literal: They said, 'We know them.'
translations.idiomatic: They replied, 'We do.'

sentences.zh: 高帝曰：「夫獵，追殺獸兔者狗也，而發蹤指示獸處者人也。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: 'In hunting, those who pursue and kill beasts and rabbits are dogs, while those who discern tracks and point out where the beasts are are humans.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, 'In a hunt, the ones who chase down and kill the game are the dogs, but the one who picks up the trail and directs the dogs to the quarry is the hunter.

sentences.zh: 今諸君徒能得走獸耳，功狗也。

translations.literal: Now you gentlemen can only catch fleeing beasts—your merit is that of dogs.
translations.idiomatic: Now, you gentlemen can only run down the game. Your merit is that of the dogs.

sentences.zh: 至如蕭何，發蹤指示，功人也。

translations.literal: As for Xiao He, he discerns tracks and points them out—his merit is that of a human.
translations.idiomatic: But Xiao He picked up the trail and pointed the way. His merit is that of the hunter.

sentences.zh: 且諸君獨以身隨我，多者兩三人。

translations.literal: Moreover, you gentlemen followed me with only your own persons, at most two or three people.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, each of you followed me with at most two or three of your kin.

sentences.zh: 今蕭何舉宗數十人皆隨我，功不可忘也。」

translations.literal: Now Xiao He raised his entire clan of several dozen people to all follow me—his merit cannot be forgotten.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He brought his entire clan of several dozen people to follow me. That kind of merit must not be forgotten.'

sentences.zh: 群臣皆莫敢言。

translations.literal: All the ministers dared not speak further.
translations.idiomatic: None of the ministers dared say another word.

sentences.zh: 列侯畢已受封，及奏位次，皆曰：「平陽侯曹參身被七十創，攻城略地，功最多，宜第一。」

translations.literal: The marquises had all received their enfeoffments, and when they memorialized about positions in order, all said: 'Marquis Pingyang Cao Shen suffered seventy wounds on his body, attacking cities and seizing territory—his merit is the greatest, he should be first.'
translations.idiomatic: After all the marquises had received their fiefs, the question of precedence arose. They all declared, 'The Marquis of Pingyang, Cao Shen, bore seventy wounds on his body, storming cities and seizing territory. His merit is the greatest; he should rank first.'

sentences.zh: 上已橈功臣，多封蕭何，至位次未有以復難之，然心欲何第一。

translations.literal: The emperor had already thwarted the meritorious ministers by greatly enfeoffing Xiao He, but regarding positions in order, there was nothing to challenge it again, yet in his heart he wished He to be first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already overruled the ministers once by granting Xiao He the largest fief. On the matter of precedence, he had no ready argument to counter them, yet in his heart he wanted Xiao He to be first.

sentences.zh: 關內侯鄂君進曰：「群臣議皆誤。

translations.literal: Marquis within the Pass E Jun advanced and said: 'The ministers' discussion is all mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: E Jun, who held the rank of Marquis within the Passes, stepped forward and said, 'The ministers are all wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫曹參雖有野戰略地之功，此特一時之事。

translations.literal: Although Cao Shen has merit in attacking cities and seizing territory in the field, this is merely the matter of a single time.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shen may have the merit of campaigning in the field and seizing territory, but these are achievements of the moment.

sentences.zh: 夫上與楚相距五歲，常失軍亡眾，逃身遁者數矣。

translations.literal: The emperor confronted Chu for five years, frequently losing troops and men, escaping and fleeing several times.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor confronted Chu for five years, repeatedly losing his army and his men, and fled for his life on more than one occasion.

sentences.zh: 然蕭何常從關中遣軍補其處，非上所詔令召，而數萬眾會上之乏絕者數矣。

translations.literal: Yet Xiao He constantly sent troops from Guanzhong to fill the gaps, not by the emperor's edict or summons, and tens of thousands gathered to supply the emperor's shortages several times.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xiao He kept dispatching troops from within the passes to fill the gaps, without any edict or summons from the emperor, and on several occasions sent tens of thousands of reinforcements to relieve the emperor's desperate shortages.

sentences.zh: 夫漢與楚相守滎陽數年，軍無見糧，蕭何轉漕關中，給食不乏。

translations.literal: Han and Chu confronted each other at Xingyang for several years, the army had no visible grain, but Xiao He transported grain from Guanzhong, supplying food without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: When Han and Chu were locked in a standoff at Xingyang for years and the army had no grain in sight, it was Xiao He who shipped provisions from within the passes, ensuring the troops never went hungry.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖數亡山東，蕭何常全關中以待陛下，此萬世之功也。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty frequently lost Shandong, Xiao He constantly preserved Guanzhong to await Your Majesty—this is merit for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty lost the lands east of the mountains time and again, Xiao He always kept the heartland within the passes intact, waiting for Your Majesty's return. This is a merit that will endure for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 今雖亡曹參等百數，何缺於漢？

translations.literal: Now even if we lacked a hundred Cao Shens and the like, what would Han lack?
translations.idiomatic: Even if we had lost a hundred men like Cao Shen, what real harm would it have done to Han?

sentences.zh: 漢得之不必待以全。

translations.literal: Han obtaining it does not necessarily depend on them for completeness.
translations.idiomatic: The survival of Han did not depend on having every last one of them.

sentences.zh: 柰何欲以一旦之功而加萬世之功哉！

translations.literal: How can one wish to place the merit of a single day above the merit of ten thousand generations!
translations.idiomatic: How can you place the merit of a single day above merit for ten thousand generations!

sentences.zh: 蕭何第一，曹參次之。」

translations.literal: Xiao He first, Cao Shen second.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He should rank first, and Cao Shen second.'

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said: 'Good.'
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, 'Well spoken.'

sentences.zh: 於是乃令蕭何［第一］，賜帶劍履上殿，入朝不趨。

translations.literal: Thus he commanded Xiao He to be first, granting him the right to wear sword and shoes on the hall, and not to hasten when entering court.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon decreed Xiao He first in rank and granted him the privilege of wearing his sword and shoes into the audience hall and of walking at his own pace when entering court.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吾聞進賢受上賞。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I have heard that advancing the worthy receives the highest reward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'I have heard it said that the one who recommends a worthy man deserves the highest reward.

sentences.zh: 蕭何功雖高，得鄂君乃益明。」

translations.literal: Though Xiao He's merit is high, obtaining E Jun makes it even clearer.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He's merit is great, but it took E Jun's words to make it shine even more clearly.'

sentences.zh: 於是因鄂君故所食關內侯邑封為安平侯。

translations.literal: Thus because of E Jun, he enfeoffed the fief households that E Jun had as Marquis within the Pass as Marquis of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore took the fief that E Jun had held as a Marquis within the Passes and elevated him to the rank of Marquis of Anping.

sentences.zh: 是日，悉封何父子兄弟十餘人，皆有食邑。

translations.literal: That day, he completely enfeoffed He's father, sons, and brothers more than ten people, all with fief households.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, the emperor enfeoffed more than ten members of Xiao He's family, including his father, sons, and brothers, granting each of them a fief.

sentences.zh: 乃益封何二千戶，以帝嘗繇咸陽時何送我獨贏錢二也。

translations.literal: He increased He's enfeoffment by two thousand households, because when the emperor was once drafted to Xianyang, He sent him extra coins alone.
translations.idiomatic: He also increased Xiao He's fief by two thousand households, in memory of the time long ago when the emperor was conscripted to Xianyang and Xiao He alone had given him two extra cash beyond what the others offered.

sentences.zh: 漢十一年，陳豨反，高祖自將，至邯鄲。

translations.literal: In Han year 11, Chen Xi rebelled. Gaozu personally led troops and arrived at Handan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Han, Chen Xi rose in rebellion. Gaozu personally led the campaign and marched to Handan.

sentences.zh: 未罷，淮陰侯謀反關中，呂后用蕭何計，誅淮陰侯，語在淮陰事中。

translations.literal: Before the campaign had ended, the Marquis of Huaiyin plotted rebellion within the passes. Empress Lü used Xiao He's plan to execute the Marquis of Huaiyin. The account is in the affairs of Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Before the campaign was over, the Marquis of Huaiyin plotted rebellion within the passes. Empress Lu used a stratagem devised by Xiao He to have the marquis executed. The details are recorded in the account of the Marquis of Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 上已聞淮陰侯誅，使使拜丞相何為相國，益封五千戶，令卒五百人一都尉為相國衛。

translations.literal: The emperor had already heard of Marquis Huaiyin's execution and sent an envoy to appoint Chancellor He as Prime Minister, increasing his enfeoffment by five thousand households, and commanding five hundred soldiers and one Commandant to guard the Prime Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of the Marquis of Huaiyin's execution, he sent a messenger to promote Chancellor He to the title of Prime Minister, increased his fief by five thousand households, and assigned five hundred soldiers under a commandant as the Prime Minister's personal guard.

sentences.zh: 諸君皆賀，召平獨弔。

translations.literal: All the ministers congratulated him, but Zhao Ping alone offered condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone offered congratulations, but Zhao Ping alone came to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 召平者，故秦東陵侯。

translations.literal: Zhao Ping was formerly the Qin Marquis of Dongling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ping had been the Marquis of Dongling under the Qin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 秦破，為布衣，貧，種瓜於長安城東，瓜美，故世俗謂之「東陵瓜」，從召平以為名也。

translations.literal: After Qin was destroyed, he became a commoner, poor, and grew melons east of Chang'an city. The melons were delicious, so the world called them 'Dongling melons,' taking the name from Zhao Ping.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin fell, he became a poor commoner and grew melons east of Chang'an. The melons were so fine that people called them 'Dongling melons' after his former title.

sentences.zh: 召平謂相國曰：「禍自此始矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Ping told the Prime Minister: 'Disaster begins from this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ping said to the Prime Minister, 'This is where your troubles begin.

sentences.zh: 上暴露於外而君守於中，非被矢石之事而益君封置衛者，以今者淮陰侯新反於中，疑君心矣。

translations.literal: The emperor is exposed abroad while you guard within. Though not suffering arrow and stone affairs, yet increasing your enfeoffment and placing guards for you—because recently Marquis Huaiyin rebelled within, he doubts your heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is enduring hardship in the field while you guard the capital. You have faced no arrows or stones, yet he increases your fief and stations guards around you. The Marquis of Huaiyin just rebelled from within the capital—the emperor now suspects your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 夫置衛衛君，非以寵君也。

translations.literal: Placing guards to guard you is not to favor you.
translations.idiomatic: The guards posted around you are not a mark of favor; they are there to watch you.

sentences.zh: 願君讓封勿受，悉以家私財佐軍，則上心說。」

translations.literal: I wish you to decline the enfeoffment and not accept it, using all your private family wealth to assist the army, then the emperor's heart will be pleased.'
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to decline the new fief and instead donate your entire personal fortune to support the army. Only then will the emperor's mind be set at ease.'

sentences.zh: 相國從其計，高帝乃大喜。

translations.literal: The Prime Minister followed his plan, and Gaozu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Prime Minister followed this advice, and Gaozu was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 漢十二年秋，黥布反，上自將擊之，數使使問相國何為。

translations.literal: In Han year 12 autumn, Ying Bu rebelled. The emperor personally led troops to attack him, frequently sending envoys to ask what the Prime Minister was doing.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twelfth year of Han, Ying Bu rose in rebellion. The emperor personally led the campaign against him, and kept sending messengers back to ask what the Prime Minister was doing.

sentences.zh: 相國為上在軍，乃拊循勉力百姓，悉以所有佐軍，如陳豨時。

translations.literal: The Prime Minister, because the emperor was in the army, stroked and encouraged the people, using all he had to assist the army, like during Chen Xi's time.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor was away at war, the Prime Minister comforted and rallied the people and poured all available resources into supporting the army, just as he had done during the campaign against Chen Xi.

sentences.zh: 客有說相國曰：「君滅族不久矣。

translations.literal: A guest advised the Prime Minister: 'Your clan will be extinguished soon.
translations.idiomatic: A retainer warned the Prime Minister, 'It will not be long before your entire clan is wiped out.

sentences.zh: 夫君位為相國，功第一，可復加哉？

translations.literal: Your position is Prime Minister, merit first—can it be increased further?
translations.idiomatic: You hold the office of Prime Minister and rank first in merit. What more could possibly be added?

sentences.zh: 然君初入關中，得百姓心，十餘年矣，皆附君，常復孳孳得民和。

translations.literal: Yet when you first entered Guanzhong, you won the people's hearts. For more than ten years, all have attached themselves to you, and you constantly diligently obtain the people's harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since you first entered the lands within the passes, you have held the hearts of the people. For more than ten years they have all rallied to you, and you have worked tirelessly to win their goodwill.

sentences.zh: 上所為數問君者，畏君傾動關中。

translations.literal: The reason the emperor frequently asks about you is that he fears you will overturn Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The reason the emperor keeps asking about you is that he fears you might stir up the lands within the passes.

sentences.zh: 今君胡不多買田地，賤貰貸以自汙？

translations.literal: Now why don't you buy more fields and land, borrow cheaply to defile yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Why not buy up large tracts of land on the cheap, even taking loans at low interest, and so tarnish your own reputation?

sentences.zh: 上心乃安。」

translations.literal: Then the emperor's heart will be at peace.'
translations.idiomatic: Then the emperor's mind will be put at ease.'

sentences.zh: 於是相國從其計，上乃大說。

translations.literal: Thus the Prime Minister followed his plan, and the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Prime Minister took this advice, and the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 上罷布軍歸，民道遮行上書，言相國賤彊買民田宅數千萬。

translations.literal: The emperor disbanded the Bu army and returned. People along the road intercepted him to submit memorials, saying the Prime Minister forcibly bought people's fields and houses cheaply for tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from defeating Ying Bu, people along the road blocked his procession to present petitions, accusing the Prime Minister of using his power to buy up their fields and houses at low prices, spending tens of millions in all.

sentences.zh: 上至，相國謁。

translations.literal: When the emperor arrived, the Prime Minister made his audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached the capital, the Prime Minister came to present himself at court.

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「夫相國乃利民！」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed: 'The Prime Minister is benefiting the people!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, 'So the Prime Minister has been looking after the people's interests!'

sentences.zh: 民所上書皆以與相國，曰：「君自謝民。」

translations.literal: He gave all the people's submitted memorials to the Prime Minister, saying: 'You personally apologize to the people.'
translations.idiomatic: He handed all the people's petitions to the Prime Minister and said, 'You can apologize to them yourself.'

sentences.zh: 相國因為民請曰：「長安地狹，上林中多空地，棄，願令民得入田，毋收槁為禽獸食。」

translations.literal: The Prime Minister thus petitioned for the people: 'Chang'an land is narrow. In Shanglin Park there is much empty land, abandoned. I wish to allow people to enter and farm it, not collecting the stubble for birds and beasts to eat.'
translations.idiomatic: The Prime Minister then petitioned on behalf of the people, saying, 'The farmland around Chang'an is scarce. There is much vacant land lying unused in the Shanglin Park. I ask that the people be allowed to enter and cultivate it, leaving the stubble in the fields as fodder for the wild animals rather than collecting it.'

sentences.zh: 上大怒曰：「相國多受賈人財物，乃為請吾苑！」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered: 'The Prime Minister has received much wealth from merchants, and thus petitions for my park!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, saying, 'The Prime Minister has taken bribes from the merchants, and now he dares petition for my royal park!'

sentences.zh: 乃下相國廷尉，械系之。

translations.literal: He sent the Prime Minister to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement, shackling and binding him.
translations.idiomatic: He had the Prime Minister handed over to the Commandant of Justice, who clapped him in fetters and chains.

sentences.zh: 數日，王衛尉侍，前問曰：「相國何大罪，陛下系之暴也？」

translations.literal: Several days later, Wang Weiwei attended and asked before him: 'What great crime has the Prime Minister committed that Your Majesty shackles him so violently?'
translations.idiomatic: Several days later, the Commandant of the Palace Guard, Wang, was in attendance and ventured to ask, 'What terrible crime has the Prime Minister committed that Your Majesty treats him so harshly?'

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吾聞李斯相秦皇帝，有善歸主，有惡自與。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I have heard that when Li Si served as chancellor under the First Emperor of Qin, he attributed good deeds to his ruler and took failings upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, 'I have heard that when Li Si served as chancellor under the First Emperor of Qin, he credited every good deed to his ruler and took every failing upon himself.

sentences.zh: 今相國多受賈豎金而為民請吾苑，以自媚於民，故系治之。」

translations.literal: Now the Prime Minister has received much gold from merchants and petitions for my park on behalf of the people, to curry favor with the people, thus I shackle and investigate him.'
translations.idiomatic: Now the Prime Minister has accepted gold from petty merchants and then petitioned for my park on behalf of the people, all to ingratiate himself with them. That is why I have had him arrested and put under investigation.'

sentences.zh: 王衛尉曰：「夫職事茍有便於民而請之，真宰相事，陛下柰何乃疑相國受賈人錢乎！

translations.literal: Wang Weiwei said: 'If in one's duties one petitions for what benefits the people, that is truly a prime minister's affair. How can Your Majesty doubt that the Prime Minister received merchants' money!
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant Wang said, 'If a minister discovers something that would benefit the people and petitions for it, that is precisely what a prime minister ought to do. How can Your Majesty suspect the Prime Minister of taking merchants' bribes?

sentences.zh: 且陛下距楚數歲，陳豨、黥布反，陛下自將而往，當是時，相國守關中，搖足則關以西非陛下有也。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty confronted Chu for several years. Chen Xi and Ying Bu rebelled. Your Majesty personally led troops there. At that time, the Prime Minister guarded Guanzhong—if he stamped his foot, west of the pass would not be yours.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty fought Chu for years, and when Chen Xi and Ying Bu rose in rebellion, Your Majesty personally led the armies against them. During all that time, the Prime Minister guarded the lands within the passes. Had he so much as stamped his foot, everything west of the passes would have ceased to be yours.

sentences.zh: 相國不以此時為利，今乃利賈人之金乎？

translations.literal: The Prime Minister did not take advantage at that time—now would he take advantage of merchants' gold?
translations.idiomatic: The Prime Minister did not seize his advantage then. Would he now stoop to profit from the gold of petty merchants?

sentences.zh: 且秦以不聞其過亡天下，李斯之分過，又何足法哉。

translations.literal: Moreover, Qin perished because they did not hear their faults. Li Si's sharing of faults—what is there to emulate?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Qin lost the empire precisely because it refused to hear criticism. Li Si's practice of deflecting blame was hardly worth emulating.

sentences.zh: 陛下何疑宰相之淺也。」

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty harbor such petty suspicions of the prime minister?'
translations.idiomatic: Why does Your Majesty suspect the Prime Minister on such slight grounds?'

sentences.zh: 高帝不懌。

translations.literal: Gaozu was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was not pleased to hear this.

sentences.zh: 是日，使使持節赦出相國。

translations.literal: That day, he sent an envoy holding the tally to pardon and release the Prime Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yet that very day, he sent an envoy bearing the imperial tally to pardon and release the Prime Minister.

sentences.zh: 相國年老，素恭謹，入，徒跣謝。

translations.literal: The Prime Minister was old and usually respectful. He entered barefoot to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The Prime Minister, old and ever deferential by nature, came before the emperor barefoot to offer his apology.

sentences.zh: 高帝曰：「相國休矣！

translations.literal: Gaozu said: 'Prime Minister, that's enough!
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, 'Enough, Prime Minister!

sentences.zh: 相國為民請苑，吾不許，我不過為桀紂主，而相國為賢相。

translations.literal: The Prime Minister petitions for the park on behalf of the people. I do not permit it. I am merely a Jie or Zhou ruler, while the Prime Minister is a worthy chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: You petitioned for the park on behalf of the people, and I refused. That only makes me a tyrant like Jie or Zhou, while you are a worthy minister.

sentences.zh: 吾故系相國，欲令百姓聞吾過也。」

translations.literal: I therefore shackled the Prime Minister to make the people hear of my faults.'
translations.idiomatic: I had you arrested deliberately, so that the people would hear of my faults.'

sentences.zh: 何素不與曹參相能，及何病，孝惠自臨視相國病，因問曰：「君即百歲後，誰可代君者？」

translations.literal: He normally did not get along with Cao Shen. When He fell ill, Emperor Hui personally visited to see the Prime Minister's illness, and asked: 'If you pass away after a hundred years, who can replace you?'
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He and Cao Shen had never been on good terms. When Xiao He fell gravely ill, Emperor Hui came personally to visit him at his sickbed and asked, 'When you are gone, who could take your place?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「知臣莫如主。」

translations.literal: He replied: 'No one knows a minister better than his ruler.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He replied, 'No one knows his ministers better than their lord.'

sentences.zh: 孝惠曰：「曹參何如？」

translations.literal: Emperor Hui said: 'What about Cao Shen?'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui asked, 'What do you think of Cao Shen?'

sentences.zh: 何頓首曰：「帝得之矣！

translations.literal: He bowed his head to the ground and said, 'Your Majesty has found the right man!
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He bowed his head to the ground and said, 'Your Majesty has found the right man!

sentences.zh: 臣死不恨矣！」

translations.literal: I will die without regret!'
translations.idiomatic: I can die without regret.'

sentences.zh: 何置田宅必居窮處，為家不治垣屋。

translations.literal: When He acquired fields and houses, he always lived in poor places. For his household, he did not repair walls or roofs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xiao He bought land or a house, he always chose an out-of-the-way location, and he never bothered to repair the walls or roof of his home.

sentences.zh: 曰：「後世賢，師吾儉；

translations.literal: He said: 'If later generations are worthy, they will emulate my frugality;
translations.idiomatic: He said, 'If my descendants prove worthy, they will follow the example of my frugality.

sentences.zh: 不賢，毋為勢家所奪。」

translations.literal: if not worthy, do not let powerful families seize it.'
translations.idiomatic: If they prove unworthy, at least the property will be too mean for powerful families to bother seizing.'

sentences.zh: 孝惠二年，相國何卒，謚為文終侯。

translations.literal: In Emperor Hui's second year, Prime Minister He died and was given the posthumous title Marquis Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Hui's reign, Prime Minister Xiao He passed away. He was given the posthumous title of Marquis Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 後嗣以罪失侯者四世，絕，天子輒復求何後，封續酂侯，功臣莫得比焉。

translations.literal: His descendants lost the marquisate due to crimes for four generations, and the line was extinguished. The Son of Heaven always sought He's descendants again, enfeoffing them to continue the Cuo marquisate. No other meritorious minister could compare.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants lost the title through offenses over four successive generations and the line was extinguished, yet each time the Son of Heaven sought out Xiao He's heirs and restored them to the marquisate of Zan. No other minister of merit was ever treated with such honor.

sentences.zh: 太史公曰：蕭相國何於秦時為刀筆吏，錄錄未有奇節。

translations.literal: The Grand Historian says: Prime Minister Xiao He during Qin times was a clerk, mediocre without exceptional conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian remarks: Chancellor Xiao He served as a petty clerk under the Qin, an unremarkable man with no record of extraordinary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 及漢興，依日月之末光，何謹守管籥，因民之疾（奉）［秦］法，順流與之更始。

translations.literal: When Han arose, relying on the reflected light of the new sovereigns, he carefully guarded the keys of state, taking advantage of the people's hatred of Qin laws, flowing with the current to make a new beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the Han dynasty arose, he rode in the reflected glory of the new order, faithfully guarding the keys of state. He seized upon the people's hatred of the harsh Qin laws, followed the current of the times, and helped bring about a fresh beginning.

sentences.zh: 淮陰、黥布等皆以誅滅，而何之勳爛焉。

translations.literal: Huaiyin, Ying Bu and others were all executed and perished, while He's merit shines brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Huaiyin, Ying Bu, and the others all met their end by execution, but Xiao He's merit shone ever more brightly.

sentences.zh: 位冠群臣，聲施後世，與閎夭、散宜生等爭烈矣。

translations.literal: His position crowned all ministers, his reputation extends to later generations, contending with Hong Yao, San Yisheng and others in glory.
translations.idiomatic: He stood first among all the ministers, and his fame has endured through the ages, rivaling in splendor that of Hong Yao, San Yisheng, and the other great ministers of antiquity.
